━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📊 UNDERSTANDING THE COT REPORT — YOUR WEEKLY EDGE

The Commitment of Traders report is released every Friday by the CFTC. It shows you exactly what the big players are doing with their money.

Three groups matter:

- Commercial Hedgers: Banks and institutions protecting positions. When they go heavily short on 10-Year Treasury futures, they often see rates rising ahead.

- Large Speculators: Hedge funds hunting profits. Their extreme positioning often marks turning points.

- Small Traders: Retail crowd. Usually wrong at extremes.

Real Example: In late August 2026, Large Speculators held record net short positions in 30-Year Bond futures while Commercials were aggressively long. Two weeks later, yields dropped 40 basis points as the smart money was proven right.

How to use it:

- Check positioning extremes. When speculators are 90 percent net long or short, watch for reversals.
- Follow the Commercials. They have inside knowledge of actual supply and demand.
- Combine with price action. COT data is delayed by three days, so confirm with current charts.

PRO TIP: Focus on the rate of change in positioning, not just absolute numbers. A rapid shift by Commercials signals conviction.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🌊 ELLIOTT WAVE BASICS — COUNTING THE MARKET'S RHYTHM

Markets move in predictable patterns. Elliott Wave Theory maps these movements into five waves up, three waves down.

The Structure:

- Wave 1: Initial move. Often small, easily missed.
- Wave 2: Pullback. Scares out weak hands.
- Wave 3: The monster. Longest and strongest. Never the shortest.
- Wave 4: Correction again. Usually sideways or shallow.
- Wave 5: Final push. Often shows divergence on indicators.

Then comes ABC correction:

- Wave A: Down hard.
- Wave B: Fake rally that traps buyers.
- Wave C: Capitulation move that completes the correction.

Real Example: German Bund futures in July 2026 showed a textbook five-wave rally from 128.50 to 134.20 over six weeks. Wave 3 covered 320 ticks, wave 1 only 180 ticks. The ABC correction that followed brought price back to 131.80 before the next impulse.

Trading Application:

- Enter on wave 2 pullbacks after confirming wave 1.
- Hold through wave 3 for maximum profit.
- Exit before wave 5 completes. Fifth waves often fail expectations.
- Never buy wave B in a correction. It is a trap.

SMART MONEY RULE: Wave 3 must be the longest or wave 5 will likely disappoint. Plan accordingly.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 THREE TIPS FOR MONDAY 14 SEPTEMBER 2026

1. Watch Central Bank Week Ahead
   Multiple central banks speak this week including Fed and ECB officials. Bond markets hate surprises. Review the speech calendar Sunday night. Volatility spikes around hawkish or dovish comments. Tighten stops on existing Treasury or Gilt positions before scheduled speakers.

2. Avoid Overtrading After Weekends
   Monday gaps in bond futures often fill by midday London session. If US 10-Year futures gap up or down at open, wait 90 minutes. Let the initial emotion clear. The best setups appear after 10:30 AM ET when real institutional flow begins.

3. Check Yield Curve Spreads
   The 2-Year to 10-Year spread tells you what smart money expects. Flattening curve means recession fears or rate cut expectations. Steepening means growth optimism. This context beats any single indicator. Check it before placing directional trades on any maturity.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🛡️ MONEY MANAGEMENT — THE MATH THAT SAVES ACCOUNTS

Risk management is not optional. It is the difference between surviving and blowing up.

The 2 Percent Rule:

Never risk more than 2 percent of your account on a single trade. If you have 10,000 dollars, max loss per trade is 200 dollars. This means you can be wrong 10 times in a row and still have 80 percent of your capital.

Position Sizing Formula:

Account Size x Risk Percent / Stop Loss in Dollars = Position Size

Example: 50,000 dollar account, 1.5 percent risk, 150 tick stop on ZN futures (10-Year Notes at 15.625 dollars per tick).

50,000 x 0.015 / 234.37 = 3.2 contracts (round to 3)

Why This Matters:

Most traders focus on entries and ignore sizing. You can have a 40 percent win rate and still be profitable with proper 3:1 reward-risk ratios. But with bad position sizing, even 70 percent win rates blow accounts.

Additional Rules:

- Never increase size after losses to recover faster. That is revenge trading.
- Scale down during drawdowns. If down 10 percent, cut risk to 1 percent per trade.
- Correlated trades count as one position. Long TLT and short interest rate futures is the same bet twice.

PRO TIP: Write your maximum risk on a sticky note on your monitor. Check it before every entry. Discipline beats intelligence in trading.
